title: Cochain upper truncations compared coherently with derived truncations
statement: For an abelian category C with a derived category, localization of the cochain upper smart truncation at q is uniquely isomorphic to the canonical derived truncation below q+1, subject to commuting with the inclusions into Q(K). The same normalized comparison is proved in the bounded-below cochain and derived categories, using the fully faithful derived inclusion. Actual cutoff maps are constructed and shown unique, and the comparisons assemble into a natural isomorphism of the entire finite-cutoff towers, natural also in complex maps. Each isomorphism is constructed from a proved unique characterization. It is natural in every complex map and commutes with every map between cutoffs whose composite with the upper inclusion is the lower inclusion.

proof.text: The cochain truncation short exact sequence gives a distinguished triangle. Its first object is at most q. Its third object maps by a quasi-isomorphism to the lower truncation at q+1 and is therefore at least q+1. Compare it with the canonical t-structure triangle by triangle_iso_exists, using the identity on Q(K).

The first component commutes with the inclusions. The t-structure to_truncLT_obj_ext principle gives uniqueness, since maps from an object at most q to the upper truncation are determined by their composites with the inclusion.

For the bounded-below version, compare the same cochain truncation triangle with the image of the canonical D+ triangle under the fully faithful inclusion. The localization comparison supplies the middle isomorphism. The first component, preceded by the localization comparison on the truncated complex, lifts through the fully faithful inclusion. Its inclusion equation follows from the triangle square and localization naturality. The D+ truncation extensionality principle proves uniqueness.

For q less than r, lift the smaller truncation inclusion in every degree below r through the coordinate isomorphism of the larger truncation; at or above r the source is zero. Cancel the larger monic inclusion to prove the chain-map equation and uniqueness. Equal cutoffs use identity. The inclusion equations prove the identity, composition and complex-map naturality laws. These maps form the actual finite-cutoff cochain tower.

Choose the comparison from this proved unique characterization. Apply the same extensionality principle to a complex map or to a cutoff inclusion. The normalization equations and naturality of the truncation inclusion prove the required squares.
